attribution.note: Marcus's own footnote on his Substack, answering his own question in his own voice. Endorsed, not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: Fair summary of a present-state judgment. 'Would surely' is high confidence, not a hedge. The domestic-humanoid scope and the assumption that motor control is solved are kept.

contract.note: The plain reading (no reliable, safe general household decision-maker, with motor skills assumed) is ordinary and fair. The speaker set no threshold for viability, so the result depends on the evaluator's reading. The contract correctly says missing demonstrations alone cannot prove the claim.

evidence.note: Google's own August 2022 report: 74% execution success on 101 tasks in two kitchens. Shows limited LLM-driven household ability. It tests neither general household competence nor safety, so it neither proves nor refutes the claim.
September 2022 preprint showing LLMs writing robot control code. Shows useful narrow ability but says nothing about safe, general domestic operation.
May 2022 Gato paper calls the work proof-of-concept with no user deployment. Fits the claim of limited readiness but does not show that every option was inadequate.

reviews.rationale: The evidence shows LLM-based robot systems with narrow household-task ability in 2022 and generalist agents still at proof-of-concept stage. Nothing documents a safe, adequate general household controller, which would contradict the claim. But nothing establishes that AlphaStar or LLMs were inadequate and unsafe for this role, and the packet's own stated gaps say so. Under the contract, missing demonstrations are not enough to support the claim. The packet does not settle it.
